name: PowerShell Disk Report (Cronsole)
description: Print free space for every fixed drive on the Cronsole host, so the numbers land in the run history and you can read them back over time.

nativeJob.body:
# Needs PowerShell on the machine running the Cronsole backend.
# That is your desktop for a normal install, and the CONTAINER on a
# Dockerized stack — where these drives are the container’s, not yours.

Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DriveType=3" |
  ForEach-Object {
    $freeGb  = [math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1)
    $totalGb = [math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 1)
    "{0} {1} GB free of {2} GB" -f $_.DeviceID, $freeGb, $totalGb
  }

parameters.label: Arguments
parameters.help: Optional command-line arguments.

name: Scan a Log for Errors
description: Search a log file for a pattern and fail the run when it matches, so a job that writes its problems to a file instead of alerting you still turns into something you can see. Supply the log to read and the text or regular expression that counts as trouble.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: The file to search. A wildcard such as C:\logs\*.log reads every matching file.

parameters.label: Pattern that means trouble
parameters.help: Text or a regular expression. A match exits non-zero, which Cronsole records as a failed run. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

name: Scheduled Reboot (Windows)
description: Restart the machine on a schedule after a warning delay — useful for applying pending updates during a maintenance window. Signs out every session, so schedule it only when no one is expected to be active.

parameters.label: Warning delay (seconds)
parameters.help: How long signed-in users see the restart warning before it happens.

parameters.label: Restart message
parameters.help: Text shown in the shutdown warning dialog. Avoid quote characters.

name: Scheduled Test Run (npm)
description: Run a project test suite on a schedule and capture the log; a red run means failing tests.

parameters.label: Project path
parameters.help: Folder containing package.json (avoid spaces in the path).

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to write the test output.

name: Send an Email Alert (SMTP)
description: Send a scheduled email through an SMTP relay using PowerShell — an alert channel for anyone who wants a message in their inbox rather than a chat webhook.

parameters.label: SMTP server
parameters.help: Hostname or IP of an SMTP relay that accepts mail from this machine without authentication, such as an internal relay or your mail provider’s relay endpoint.

parameters.label: From address
parameters.help: The address the alert appears to come from.

parameters.label: To address
parameters.help: Where to send the alert.

parameters.label: Subject
parameters.help: The email subject line. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

parameters.label: Body
parameters.help: The email body text. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

name: Send an SMS Alert (Twilio)
description: Send a scheduled text message through the Twilio API — an alert channel for anyone who wants a message on their phone rather than a chat webhook or an email.

parameters.label: Twilio Account SID
parameters.help: Found on the Twilio Console dashboard.

parameters.label: Twilio Auth Token
parameters.help: Found on the Twilio Console dashboard. Treat it like a password.

parameters.label: From number
parameters.help: A Twilio phone number on your account, in E.164 format (e.g. +15551234567).

parameters.label: To number
parameters.help: The phone number to text, in E.164 format.

parameters.label: Message
parameters.help: The SMS body. Keep it short — long messages are billed as multiple segments.

name: Shell Script (bash)
description: Run a shell script with bash on macOS or Linux.

parameters.label: Script file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the script on the target machine.

parameters.label: Arguments
parameters.help: Optional command-line arguments.

name: Shell Script (zsh)
description: Run a shell script with zsh, the macOS default shell.

parameters.label: Script file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the script on the target machine.

parameters.label: Arguments
parameters.help: Optional command-line arguments.

name: Slack Webhook Message
description: Post a scheduled message to a Slack channel through an Incoming Webhook URL.

parameters.label: Slack webhook URL
parameters.help: Create one from Slack: Apps -> Incoming Webhooks -> Add New Webhook, then copy the URL for the channel.

parameters.label: Message
parameters.help: The text to post. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

name: SSL Certificate Expiry Check (Cronsole)
description: Connect to a host over TLS and fail the run when its certificate expires within your warning window. Cronsole has no certificate probe yet, so this uses a Node script and the built-in tls module rather than a check job.

parameters.label: Host
parameters.help: Hostname to connect to, resolved from the machine running the Cronsole backend.

parameters.label: Port
parameters.help: TLS port to connect to.

parameters.label: Warn within (days)
parameters.help: Fail the run when fewer than this many days remain before the certificate expires.

name: Sync Folder to Cloud (rclone)
description: Sync a local folder to a configured rclone remote (S3, Drive, B2, …).

parameters.label: Local source
parameters.help: Local path to sync from. Requires rclone installed + a configured remote.

parameters.label: Remote destination
parameters.help: rclone remote target, e.g. mydrive:backups/photos.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where rclone writes its run log.

name: Transcode Video (ffmpeg)
description: Re-encode a video file to H.264 with ffmpeg on the machine hosting Cronsole, useful for shrinking recordings dropped into a watch folder before they pile up on disk.

parameters.label: Source video path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the source video file, as seen by the machine running the Cronsole backend. ffmpeg must already be on that machine’s PATH.

parameters.label: Output video path
parameters.help: Where to write the transcoded file. Must be a different path than the source — ffmpeg cannot write over the file it is reading.

parameters.label: CRF quality
parameters.help: The x264 CRF value. Lower means higher quality and a larger file; 18 to 28 is the usual range.

name: Trigger Windows Update Scan
description: Kick off a Windows Update detection scan on a schedule.

name: Trigger: Daily Digest by Email
description: A Gemini trigger that researches a topic every morning and emails the digest through one of your saved MCP servers -- the credential stays on the connection and is never retyped.
command: Research {{topic}} and write a digest of what changed in the last 24 hours. Keep it to the {{length}} form: the developments that matter, one sentence each, with the source link. Then email it to {{recipient}} with the subject "{{topic}} digest" using the email tool available to you. Do not ask which stories to include or which address to use, both are given above. If the research or the send fails, say so explicitly in your final message and name the step that failed rather than summarizing what you would have sent.
commandTemplate: Research {{topic}} and write a digest of what changed in the last 24 hours. Keep it to the {{length}} form: the developments that matter, one sentence each, with the source link. Then email it to {{recipient}} with the subject "{{topic}} digest" using the email tool available to you. Do not ask which stories to include or which address to use, both are given above. If the research or the send fails, say so explicitly in your final message and name the step that failed rather than summarizing what you would have sent.

parameters.label: Topic
parameters.help: What to research each morning, e.g. Postgres release notes and CVEs.

parameters.label: Digest length
parameters.help: How much detail to include.

parameters.label: Send to
parameters.help: The address the digest is emailed to.

parameters.label: Email MCP server
parameters.help: The name of a saved MCP server on your Gemini connection that can send mail. Save one on the Sources tab first -- the token lives there, not in this template.

name: Trigger: Page Watch
description: A Gemini trigger that reads one page every day and reports only what changed since yesterday -- a pricing page, a status page, a changelog.
command: Read {{pageUrl}} and describe what changed since your previous run, paying attention to {{watchFor}}. Report the changes only. If nothing relevant changed, say no change in one line rather than restating the page, and quote the old and new wording for anything that did change. If the page could not be loaded, say so explicitly: an unreachable page is not the same as an unchanged one.
commandTemplate: Read {{pageUrl}} and describe what changed since your previous run, paying attention to {{watchFor}}. Report the changes only. If nothing relevant changed, say no change in one line rather than restating the page, and quote the old and new wording for anything that did change. If the page could not be loaded, say so explicitly: an unreachable page is not the same as an unchanged one.

parameters.label: Page URL
parameters.help: The page to watch, e.g. a pricing, status or changelog page.

parameters.label: Watch for
parameters.default: prices, plan limits and anything marked new or deprecated
parameters.help: What on the page matters, so an unrelated edit is not reported as news.

name: Trigger: Weekly Repo Report
description: A Gemini trigger that reads a public repository once a week and reports what shipped, what stalled, and what a user of the project would notice.
command: Read {{repoUrl}} and report on the last seven days: what merged, what is still open and has stopped moving, and any release or breaking change a user of the project would notice. Write it as short plain sentences grouped under those three headings, each entry with the pull request or issue it came from. Judge staleness by the dates on the page rather than asking what counts as stalled. If the repository cannot be read, say that explicitly instead of reporting an empty week.
commandTemplate: Read {{repoUrl}} and report on the last seven days: what merged, what is still open and has stopped moving, and any release or breaking change a user of the project would notice. Write it as short plain sentences grouped under those three headings, each entry with the pull request or issue it came from. Judge staleness by the dates on the page rather than asking what counts as stalled. If the repository cannot be read, say that explicitly instead of reporting an empty week.

parameters.label: Repository URL
parameters.help: The public repository to read, e.g. https://github.com/owner/name.

name: Upload File via SCP
description: Copy a local file to a remote server over SSH with scp, useful for shipping a report or backup off-box on a schedule.

parameters.label: Local file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the file to upload.

parameters.label: Remote destination
parameters.help: SSH destination in user@host:/path form, e.g. deploy@example.com:/backups/. Key-based authentication must already work for this user with no password prompt.

name: Uptime Check (Cronsole)
description: Call a URL every few minutes and record whether it answered. Runs in Cronsole itself — no agent, and it works on a machine with no Task Scheduler.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to GET. A non-2xx response is recorded as a failed run, which is what makes this a check rather than a ping.

name: VBScript (legacy)
description: Run a legacy .vbs script via cscript.

parameters.label: Script file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the script on the target machine.

name: Webhook / HTTP Ping (macOS)
description: Call a URL on a schedule using curl.

parameters.label: HTTP method
parameters.help: HTTP verb for the request.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to call.

name: Webhook / HTTP Ping (Windows)
description: Call a URL on a schedule using Invoke-WebRequest.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to call.

parameters.label: HTTP method
parameters.help: HTTP verb for the request.

name: Weekly System Cleanup
description: Delete temporary files on a schedule to reclaim disk space.

parameters.label: Path to clean
parameters.help: Files/glob to delete, e.g. %temp%\*.

name: Write a Script (Cronsole)
description: A starting point for a scheduled script you write in Cronsole itself. Nothing needs to exist on disk — the body is stored with the task and runs under the interpreter you pick.
